traditions/iglesia-ni-cristo/summary: A Filipino church registered in 1914 by Felix Y. Manalo, who had been a member of several Protestant churches including the Seventh-day Adventists. It teaches that the original church apostatised and was re-established through Manalo as God's last messenger. It rejects the Trinity, holding that Jesus is the Son of God and Saviour but not God, and so stands outside historic Nicene Christianity. It is noted for disciplined membership, monumental chapels and bloc voting.
traditions/iglesia-ni-cristo/distinctive: Membership in the INC necessary for salvation
traditions/iglesia-ni-cristo/profile/aut: Scripture as interpreted by the church's Executive Minister.
traditions/iglesia-ni-cristo/profile/sal: Salvation through membership in the true Church of Christ and obedience.
traditions/iglesia-ni-cristo/profile/sac: Baptism by immersion and the Holy Supper (annual).
traditions/iglesia-ni-cristo/profile/esc: Judgment Day with salvation for faithful members.
traditions/iglesia-ni-cristo/profile/wor: Twice-weekly worship with doctrinal sermons and choirs.
traditions/iglesia-ni-cristo/status: Active; large in the Philippines and the Filipino diaspora.
traditions/true-jesus-church/summary: An independent Chinese church founded in Beijing in 1917 by Paul Wei (Wei Enbo) and others, combining Oneness Pentecostal theology with Saturday Sabbath observance. It holds itself to be the restored true church. Strong in Taiwan and among Chinese communities worldwide, it was absorbed into the Three-Self structure on the mainland but continues independently elsewhere.
traditions/true-jesus-church/distinctive: Baptism by face-down immersion in natural water in Jesus' name
traditions/true-jesus-church/profile/aut: Scripture as the only basis; claims restored apostolic church.
traditions/true-jesus-church/profile/sal: Salvation requires baptism, Spirit baptism with tongues and keeping the Sabbath.
traditions/true-jesus-church/profile/sac: Water baptism, feet washing and Holy Communion.
traditions/true-jesus-church/profile/wor: Prayer in tongues together, preaching and hymns.
traditions/local-churches/name: Local Churches (Watchman Nee and Witness Lee)
traditions/local-churches/summary: A Chinese church movement that began in Fuzhou in the early 1920s around Watchman Nee, influenced by the Brethren and Keswick teaching, holding that there should be one church per city. Nee was imprisoned by the Communist government from 1952 until his death in 1972. Witness Lee carried the movement to Taiwan (1949) and the United States (1962). Some evangelical critics accused Lee's teachings of modalism and other errors; the Christian Research Institute retracted its earlier criticism in 2009, though others still dissent.
traditions/local-churches/distinctives/1: Inner life and the spirit (Nee's The Normal Christian Life)
traditions/local-churches/distinctives/2: 'Calling on the name of the Lord' and 'pray-reading' Scripture
traditions/local-churches/profile/author: Scripture, read through the ministry of Watchman Nee and Witness Lee.
traditions/local-churches/profile/salvat: Salvation by grace and the dispensing of the divine life into believers.
traditions/local-churches/profile/sacram: Baptism by immersion and the Lord's table.
traditions/local-churches/profile/eschat: Premillennial; the overcomers and the kingdom.
traditions/local-churches/profile/govern: Elders in each local church; no denominational office.
traditions/local-churches/profile/worshi: Mutual participation, calling on the Lord and pray-reading.
traditions/local-churches/status: Active in China (often unregistered), Taiwan and elsewhere.
traditions/three-self-patriotic-movement: Three-Self Patriotic Movement and China Christian Council

The state-registered Protestant church structure of the People's Republic of China, based on the 'three-self' principles (self-government, self-support, self-propagation) of earlier missionary thinking. Formalised in 1954 under Y. T. Wu after the 1950 Christian Manifesto cut ties with foreign missions, it imposed post-denominational unity. Suspended during the Cultural Revolution, it was restored in 1979, with the China Christian Council formed in 1980 under Bishop K. H. Ting. Unregistered house churches reject its accommodation to state control; supporters see it as the legal space that allowed churches to reopen.
Registration with the state Religious Affairs authorities
Scripture; preaching expected to accord with state regulations on religion.
Protestant evangelical faith in Christ in varied forms.
Baptism and the Lord's Supper in forms from former denominations.
Two national bodies (TSPM and CCC) with provincial councils, under state oversight.
Sunday services in registered churches, often crowded.
Active; tens of millions of members in registered churches.
traditions/jesus-family/summary: A communal Pentecostal-style Christian community founded by Jing Dianying, a former Methodist, at Mazhuang, Shandong, in 1927. Members pooled property, worked the land together and practised ecstatic worship. It spread to over a hundred communities before the Communist government dissolved it in 1952.
traditions/jesus-family/distinctives/3: Care for the poor and disabled
traditions/jesus-family/profile/authorit: Scripture with revelations in visions and dreams.
traditions/jesus-family/profile/salvatio: Salvation by faith expressed in total self-giving to the community.
traditions/jesus-family/profile/eschatol: Strong expectation of Christ's imminent return.
traditions/jesus-family/status: Historic; dissolved 1952, though its influence persisted in house churches.
traditions/indian-pentecostal-church-of-: Founded in Kerala in 1924 by K. E. Abraham and others who sought Indian leadership independent of foreign missionaries. Drawing many converts from Syrian Christian (Mar Thoma and Orthodox) and Dalit communities, it became one of the largest indigenous Pentecostal churches in India.
Strong in Kerala and the Gulf diaspora
Plain dress and no jewellery in many congregations
Salvation by grace; Baptism in the Holy Spirit as an experience subsequent to conversion, usually evidenced by speaking in tongues; gifts of healing and prophecy for today.
Baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper.
Pentecostal worship in Malayalam and other languages.
traditions/churches-of-christ/summary: Congregations of the Stone-Campbell movement that separated from the Disciples of Christ, recognised in the 1906 U.S. Religious Census. Reading the New Testament as a pattern for the church, they reject instrumental music in worship and organisations beyond the local congregation as unauthorised by Scripture. They see themselves not as a denomination but as the restored New Testament church.
traditions/churches-of-christ/distinctiv: Baptism by immersion for the forgiveness of sins
Autonomous congregations with no denominational headquarters
'Speak where the Bible speaks, be silent where the Bible is silent'
traditions/churches-of-christ/profile/au: The New Testament as the pattern for faith and practice: command, example and necessary inference; no creeds.
traditions/churches-of-christ/profile/sa: Hearing, believing, repenting, confessing Christ and being immersed for the remission of sins; faithful living.
Baptism by immersion of penitent believers and the Lord's Supper every Sunday.
traditions/churches-of-christ/profile/es: Mostly amillennial; Christ's return and judgment.
traditions/churches-of-christ/profile/go: Autonomous congregations led by elders and deacons; no clergy hierarchy.
traditions/churches-of-christ/profile/wo: Unaccompanied singing, weekly communion and preaching.
traditions/churches-of-christ/status: Active; non-institutional and other sub-fellowships exist.
traditions/christian-church-disciples/su: The ecumenical, mainline branch of the Stone-Campbell movement, dating its unity to the 1832 union of Barton Stone's 'Christians' and Alexander Campbell's 'Disciples'. After the Churches of Christ separated (1906) and the independent Christian Churches drifted away, it restructured as a denomination in 1968. It practises open weekly communion and was a founding member of the World Council of Churches; in 2005 Sharon Watkins became the first woman to lead a U.S. mainline denomination.
traditions/christian-church-disciples/di: Weekly open communion at the centre of worship
Commitment to Christian unity (Council on Christian Unity)
Ecumenical partnership with the United Church of Christ (1989)
traditions/christian-church-disciples/pr: Scripture and the confession that Jesus is the Christ; freedom of interpretation.
Salvation by grace through faith in Christ.
Believer's baptism by immersion, with members received from other churches; the Lord's Supper weekly, open to all.
Congregational with regions and a General Assembly (restructure 1968).
Lay elders preside at the table alongside ordained ministers.
traditions/christian-church-disciples/st: Active; declining membership typical of mainline churches.
traditions/christian-churches-churches-o: Christian Churches and Churches of Christ (independent)

Independent congregations of the Stone-Campbell movement, theologically conservative and using instrumental music, that distanced themselves from the Disciples over liberal theology, open membership and denominational structures. The North American Christian Convention (1927) gave them a forum, and they were listed separately from the Disciples by 1971. Many large evangelical megachurches belong to this fellowship.
Faith, repentance and immersion as the response to the gospel.
Believers' immersion and weekly Lord's Supper.
Contemporary evangelical worship with weekly communion.
traditions/community-of-christ/summary: The Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints, organised by Latter Day Saints who rejected Brigham Young's leadership and polygamy; Joseph Smith III became its prophet-president at Amboy, Illinois, in 1860. Headquartered in Independence, Missouri, it has moved toward mainstream Protestant theology: it ordains women (1984), practises open communion (1994), affirms the Trinity, and treats the Book of Mormon as scripture without making it a test of faithfulness. Renamed in 2001.
traditions/community-of-christ/distincti: Ongoing revelation added to its Doctrine and Covenants
Temple in Independence dedicated to peace (1994)
Mission focused on peace and justice
Never practised polygamy as a church
traditions/community-of-christ/profile/a: Scripture (Bible) with the Book of Mormon and its Doctrine and Covenants, interpreted through Christ and continuing revelation through the prophet-president.
traditions/community-of-christ/profile/s: Salvation by grace through faith in Jesus Christ, expressed in discipleship and community.
Eight sacraments: baptism, confirmation, Lord's Supper, marriage, blessing of children, ordination, laying on of hands for the sick and evangelist blessing.
traditions/community-of-christ/profile/e: Hope for the peaceable kingdom (Zion) on earth.
traditions/community-of-christ/profile/g: Prophet-president, First Presidency, Council of Twelve and World Conference.
traditions/community-of-christ/profile/c: The Bible, the Book of Mormon and the Community of Christ Doctrine and Covenants.
traditions/community-of-christ/status: Active; a few hundred thousand members worldwide.
traditions/christadelphians/summary: A lay movement founded by John Thomas, an English-born physician in the Campbell movement who was re-immersed in 1847 after concluding that baptism must follow understanding of the gospel of the Kingdom. The name 'Christadelphians' ('brothers in Christ') was adopted in 1864 to register as conscientious objectors during the U.S. Civil War. Robert Roberts of Birmingham organised the British ecclesias. They reject the Trinity, the pre-existence of Christ and the immortality of the soul, standing outside historic Nicene orthodoxy.
traditions/christadelphians/distinctives: One God, the Father; Jesus the Son of God, not pre-existent
Holy Spirit as God's power, not a person
Mortality of the soul and resurrection at Christ's return
Kingdom of God on earth centred on Israel
traditions/christadelphians/profile/auth: Scripture alone, interpreted through the Birmingham Amended Statement of Faith (1898) in many ecclesias.
traditions/christadelphians/profile/salv: Belief of the gospel of the Kingdom and the name of Jesus, followed by immersion, and a faithful life.
traditions/christadelphians/profile/sacr: Baptism by immersion of informed believers and weekly breaking of bread.
traditions/christadelphians/profile/esch: Premillennial: Christ will return to raise and judge the responsible and reign from Jerusalem; the wicked perish.
traditions/christadelphians/profile/gove: Autonomous ecclesias with elected arranging brethren.
traditions/christadelphians/profile/wors: Simple memorial meeting and Bible exposition.
